## Phase 1 — API Contract & Data Model

**Goal:** Agree the (internal, config-file-facing) Zod contract before any service code is written.
**Deliverable:** `RouteConfigSchema` and the `RouteConfig` type in sync, no running proxy logic yet.

- [ ] **Task 1.1 (T-01):** Add `RouteConfigSchema` to new file `src/schemas/route.schemas.ts`
  - Files affected: `src/schemas/route.schemas.ts` (new)
  - Fields: `path`, `upstream: string (url)`, `auth_required: boolean`, `required_scope: string | null`, `allowed_roles: string[] | null`, `rate_limit_override: number | null`, `strip_prefix: boolean`, `timeout_ms: number (default 30000)`, `audit_allowed_requests: boolean (default false)`
  - Reference: FR-16, spec's Zod Schema Changes section
  - Complexity: S | Depends on: —

- [ ] **Task 1.2 (T-02):** Add `audit_allowed_requests: boolean` to the `RouteConfig` interface in `src/types/index.ts`
  - Files affected: `src/types/index.ts`
  - Reference: FR-16 (field was added to the spec during the Open Question 2 resolution but not yet reflected in the type)
  - Complexity: S | Depends on: — (parallel-safe with T-01)

> No `specs/openapi.yaml` changes — `RouteConfigSchema` validates a startup config file, not an API request/response body, and `/api/{service}/{path}` is already fully specced. No Drizzle migration — `audit_log` already exists.

## Phase 2 — Service & Route Implementation

**Goal:** Implement route resolution, policy enforcement, upstream dispatch, and audit integration behind the existing `/api` mount point.
**Deliverable:** All ACs (AC-25, AC-26, AC-27, AC-32, AC-36) functional and unit-tested.

- [ ] **Task 2.1 (T-03):** Add proxy-specific error classes to `src/types/errors.ts`; reconcile wire codes with `specs/openapi.yaml`
  - Files affected: `src/types/errors.ts`
  - Add: `RouteNotFoundError` (404, code `route_not_found`), `GatewayTimeoutError` (504, code `gateway_timeout`)
  - Reconcile: existing `UpstreamError` currently emits code `UPSTREAM_ERROR`, but `openapi.yaml`'s documented example for this endpoint is `bad_gateway` — align the code (either change `UpstreamError`'s code string to `bad_gateway`, or confirm with `/review`/`api-contract-checker` if `UPSTREAM_ERROR` was an intentional divergence elsewhere before changing it)
  - Reference: FR-19, FR-20, `openapi.yaml` `/api/{service}/{path}` response examples
  - Complexity: S | Depends on: — (parallel-safe with T-01/T-02)

- [ ] **Task 2.2 (T-04):** Implement route-config loader
  - Files affected: `src/config/routes.ts` (new), an illustrative example routes JSON for local dev/tests (per Open Question 1 resolution — no real upstream entries in this repo)
  - Reads `UPSTREAM_SERVICES_CONFIG_PATH`, parses each entry with `RouteConfigSchema` (T-01), exits the process with a non-zero code and descriptive error on invalid config
  - Reference: FR-16
  - Complexity: M | Depends on: T-01

- [ ] **Task 2.3 (T-05):** `proxy.service.ts` — route resolution, spoofed-header stripping, identity-header injection
  - Files affected: `src/services/proxy.service.ts` (new)
  - Implements: `resolveRoute(path)` (match against loaded `RouteConfig[]`, respecting `strip_prefix`), `stripSpoofedHeaders(headers)` (strips client-supplied `X-User-Id`, `X-User-Email`, `X-User-Roles`, `X-Auth-Method` unconditionally), `buildIdentityHeaders(claims)` (`X-User-Id`, `X-User-Email`, `X-User-Roles`, `X-Auth-Method`, `X-Tenant-Id` if non-null, `X-Request-Id`), forwards/augments `X-Forwarded-For`
  - Reference: FR-16, FR-17, FR-18; AC-25, AC-26, AC-27
  - Complexity: M | Depends on: T-01, T-02, T-04

- [ ] **Task 2.4 (T-06):** `proxy.service.ts` — authorization policy enforcement + denial audit
  - Files affected: `src/services/proxy.service.ts`
  - Implements: `enforceAuthorization(route, claims)` — 401 if `auth_required` and no valid token, 403 if `allowed_roles` set and no intersection, 403 `insufficient_scope` if `required_scope` not satisfied; applies `rateLimiter({ maxRequests: route.rate_limit_override })` when set; writes `proxy.request_denied` to `audit_log` unconditionally on any denial (via existing `writeAuditEvent`)
  - Reference: FR-19, FR-20; AC-32
  - Complexity: M | Depends on: T-03, T-05

- [ ] **Task 2.5 (T-07):** `proxy.service.ts` — upstream dispatch + gated allow-audit
  - Files affected: `src/services/proxy.service.ts`
  - Implements: dispatch via `http-proxy-middleware` (`createProxyMiddleware`) using per-route `upstream` + `timeout_ms`; maps upstream unreachable → `RouteNotFoundError`/`UpstreamError` (502), upstream timeout → `GatewayTimeoutError` (504); writes `proxy.request_allowed` to `audit_log` **only** when the matched route's `audit_allowed_requests` is `true` (default hot path touches `audit_log` not at all — Open Question 2 resolution)
  - Reference: FR-16, FR-20; AC-36
  - Complexity: M | Depends on: T-03, T-05

- [ ] **Task 2.6 (T-08):** Rewrite `src/routes/proxy.router.ts`
  - Files affected: `src/routes/proxy.router.ts`
  - Replace the 501 stub's catch-all handler with: strip spoofed headers → `validateAccessToken({ optional: !route.auth_required })` → `enforceAuthorization` (T-06) → inject identity headers (T-05) → dispatch (T-07) → errors forwarded via `next(err)` to the existing global `errorHandler`
  - No change needed to `src/index.ts` — `proxyRouter` is already mounted at `/api`
  - Reference: FR-17, FR-18, FR-19; AC-25, AC-26, AC-27, AC-32
  - Complexity: S | Depends on: T-05, T-06, T-07

- [ ] **Task 2.7 (T-09):** Unit tests for route config schema
  - Files affected: `tests/unit/route.schemas.test.ts`
  - Scenarios: rejects malformed route entries; `audit_allowed_requests` defaults to `false` when omitted
  - Complexity: S | Depends on: T-01 (parallel-safe with T-04–T-08)

- [ ] **Task 2.8 (T-10):** Unit tests for `ProxyService`
  - Files affected: `tests/unit/proxy.service.test.ts`
  - Scenarios (per spec Testing Strategy): resolve route by path; strip `X-User-*` headers; inject correct identity headers; handle upstream timeout; handle upstream 5xx → 502; `auth_required: false` route passes unauthenticated; `proxy.request_allowed` audit write skipped when `audit_allowed_requests` is false/omitted, issued when true
  - Mock `ioredis`/`pg` per project convention
  - Complexity: M | Depends on: T-05, T-06, T-07

- [ ] **Task 2.9 (T-11):** Integration tests for the proxy route
  - Files affected: `tests/integration/proxy.test.ts`
  - ACs covered: AC-25, AC-26, AC-27, AC-32, AC-36
  - Scenarios: authenticated pass-through w/ header injection, unauthenticated on public route, unauthenticated on private route → 401, insufficient role → 403, insufficient scope → 403, rate limit → 429, upstream timeout → 504, header stripping, `proxy.request_allowed` written only for `audit_allowed_requests: true` routes
  - Uses real Postgres + Redis via Testcontainers — do not mock
  - Complexity: M | Depends on: T-08

## Risk Register

| # | Risk | Severity | Likelihood | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|------|----------|------------|------------|-------|
| R-1 | Existing `UpstreamError` code (`UPSTREAM_ERROR`) doesn't match `openapi.yaml`'s documented `bad_gateway` wire code for this endpoint | Medium | High | Reconcile in T-03 before T-08 wires error handling; confirm via T-15 (api-contract-checker) before merge | Implementer |
| R-2 | Rate-limit-override + route-resolution + conditional audit write add to the hot path just as NFR-1 caps overhead at ≤10ms P95 | Medium | Medium | Keep `audit_allowed_requests` default `false` (already the resolved design) so the default path skips the audit write entirely; verify with T-14 (performance-reviewer) | Implementer |
| R-3 | Route path-pattern matching (`/api/users/:path*`) needs a matching engine consistent with `strip_prefix` semantics | Low | Medium | Use the same `path-to-regexp` version Express 5 already depends on rather than a second regex engine | Implementer |
| R-4 | FR-17 only lists 4 headers to strip (`X-User-Id/Email/Roles`, `X-Auth-Method`) — `X-Tenant-Id` isn't in the strip list, so a client could still forge it | Low | Low | Flag explicitly in T-12 (`/review`) for a human decision; do not silently expand scope beyond the spec's enumerated list | Implementer / Security Engineering |

## Rollback Plan

### Trigger Conditions

Roll back if any of the following occur after deployment:
- [ ] NFR-1 gateway overhead exceeds 10ms P95 on proxied routes
- [ ] 502/504 error rate on `/api/**` exceeds baseline by more than a small margin not attributable to genuine upstream outages
- [ ] `audit_log` write volume on flagged routes grows unexpectedly and threatens PostgreSQL write capacity

### Rollback Steps

**Application:**
1. Revert the PR — this feature is purely additive (new service/route/schema files; the 501 stub can be restored) and does not alter any existing endpoint's behavior.

**Database:**
- No migration to roll back — `audit_log` already existed before this feature; this feature only conditionally writes to it.
- ⚠️ **Data impact:** none — no schema change, so no orphaned-row risk.
